vectors.description: object datagram (Type Flags 0x00: object_id present, priority present) with 4-byte payload
object datagram (Type Flags 0x04: ZERO_OBJECT_ID, so no object_id field; priority present) with empty payload
object datagram (Type Flags 0x02: END_OF_GROUP, object_id present, priority present) with payload
object datagram (Type Flags 0x20: STATUS, object_id present, priority present) with end-of-group status
object datagram (Type Flags 0x08: DEFAULT_PRIORITY, object_id present) with payload

object datagram carrying no properties (Type Flags 0x00: PROPERTIES clear, object_id present, priority present) with a 4-byte payload. Section 11.3.1 says an endpoint that receives a datagram with the PROPERTIES bit set and a Properties Length of 0 MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, so an object with no properties leaves the bit clear and omits the field entirely. A subgroup stream has the opposite rule: with the header's PROPERTIES bit set, every Object carries the field and an empty one sets Properties Length to 0
object datagram (Type Flags 0x01: PROPERTIES set) with PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2 property and 2-byte payload
object datagram (Type Flags 0x20: STATUS) with end-of-track status (0x4)

object datagram whose Type Flags value 0x00 is encoded as the 2-byte varint 8000 rather than the one-byte 00. Section 1.4.1 permits non-minimal encodings and the datagram rules constrain the value, not its width, so this decodes to Type Flags 0. Section 11.4.2 words the corresponding SUBGROUP_HEADER rule as "values of 128 or greater (i.e., any value that requires more than a one-byte variable-length integer encoding)", two clauses that are not equivalent under that allowance. This corpus is permissive on receive and strict on send, so the vector is decode-only

status datagram carrying payload bytes — must close the session. Section 11.3.1: "The STATUS bit (0x20) indicates whether the datagram contains an Object Status or Object Payload." The two occupy the same position, so the four bytes after the status are not a payload this frame can hold. Identical to the datagram-status vector with those bytes appended. Bound to the endpoint profile: a relay forwards a datagram whole and needs no part of this to find where it ends
vectors.error_detail: the datagram Type Flags set the STATUS bit, so the four trailing bytes are not a payload

vectors.description: object datagram whose Type Flags set bit 4 (0x10). Section 11.3.1 lists it among the invalid values: "Values with bit 4 (0x10) set. This bit is reserved and MUST be zero." Note that SUBGROUP_HEADER requires the opposite — bit 4 MUST be 1 there — so the datagram rules do not transfer to subgroup streams. The bytes after the Type Flags are those of the datagram-4byte-payload vector, which decodes
vectors.error_detail: datagram Type Flags bit 4 (0x10) is reserved and MUST be zero

vectors.description: object datagram whose Type Flags set both STATUS (0x20) and END_OF_GROUP (0x02). Section 11.3.1 names this combination invalid
vectors.error_detail: datagram Type Flags 0x22 sets both the STATUS and END_OF_GROUP bits

vectors.description: object datagram whose Type Flags set bit 6 (0x40), which has no specified meaning for a datagram. Section 11.3.1: "Values with a bit set whose meaning is not specified" are invalid. Bit 6 is FIRST_OBJECT on a SUBGROUP_HEADER and nothing at all here
vectors.error_detail: datagram Type Flags bit 6 (0x40) has no specified meaning

vectors.description: object datagram whose Type Flags decode to 128, encoded as the minimal two-byte varint 8080. All values draft-20 defines fit in a single byte, and 128 necessarily sets bit 7, whose meaning is not specified. Unlike SUBGROUP_HEADER, Section 11.3.1 carries no explicit "values of 128 or greater" bullet; the unspecified-bit rule is what catches this
vectors.error_detail: datagram Type Flags 128 sets an unspecified bit

vectors.description: object datagram whose Type Flags set PROPERTIES (0x01) but whose Properties Length is 0. Section 11.3.1: "If an endpoint receives a datagram with the PROPERTIES bit set and an Properties Length of 0, it MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION"
vectors.error_detail: a datagram with the PROPERTIES bit set must carry a non-empty Properties structure

vectors.description: object datagram setting both STATUS (0x20) and PROPERTIES (0x01) whose Object Status is End of Group (0x3). Section 11.3.1 closes the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION "because only Normal Objects can have Properties"
vectors.error_detail: only a Normal (0x0) Object may carry Properties
unexpected end of input while reading object_id
